expectation: Membrane stain on antigen-presenting cells: macrophages, dendritic cells and B cells in the lamina propria, plus lymphoid aggregates. They should appear as scattered irregular or dendritic cells between crypts and glands, often common. Some gut epithelium can also be HLA-DR positive.
observed: A: bright dots and streaks through the mucosa, following the lamina propria between glands. B/C: a diffuse yellow haze on the epithelium and a few bright cells. D: one bright, irregular cell with processes. E: branched, dendritic HLADRA cells; many sit on CD163 cells (white) and some are green-only.
why: Distinct dendritic-shaped cells sit in the lamina propria and partly overlap CD163 macrophages, which is the expected APC pattern and not haze or debris.
notes: Clear branched APC-like cells in the stroma between glands. Many overlap CD163 and some are CD163-negative, as dendritic cells would be. There is a moderate diffuse epithelial background, but it does not hide the specific population.
